literal: Inside the battlefield, a coward's hand bright sword, inside the assembly, he who fears, his learned book.
translation: The learning of one who fears to face an assembly is like a bright sword in the hand of a coward on a battlefield.
modern: போர்க்களத்தில் பேடியின் கையில் இருக்கும் கூர்மையான வாளைப் போன்றது, அவைக்கு அஞ்சுகின்றவன் கற்ற நூல் அறிவு.
explanation: This couplet uses a vivid analogy to show the uselessness of education without courage. A bright, sharp sword (ஒள்வாள்) is a powerful weapon, but it is completely useless in the hand of a coward (பேடிகை) on a battlefield. Similarly, the books and treatises learned (கற்ற நூல்) by a person are of no value if that person is terrified of speaking before an assembly (அவையகத்து அஞ்சுமவன்). True learning requires the courage of expression to be of any practical use.
